\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{फोन} (phon)}{फोन (phon)}]{\mw{फोन} (phon) — a phone}

\label{lesson:MW-C197-phon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for an address, then the Marwadi for to send off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{फोन}}
\textbf{\mw{फोन}} — \emph{phon} — \textquotedblleft{}a phone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{फोन} \mw{मेज} \mw{माथै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{phon mej māthai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The phone is on the table.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{फोन}} (\emph{phon}) is borrowed from English \emph{phone}, short for telephone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phon}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phon}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phon mej māthai hai.} — The phone is on the table.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for an address, then the Marwadi for to send off, then say \emph{phon} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{फोन} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A phone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

One more word for reading notices and messages.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{बाजणो} (bājṇo)}{बाजणो (bājṇo)}]{\mw{बाजणो} (bājṇo) — to ring; to sound}

\label{lesson:MW-C197-bajno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a phone, then the Marwadi for a phone number.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{बाजणो}}
\textbf{\mw{बाजणो}} — \emph{bājṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to ring; to sound\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{फोन} \mw{बाजै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{phon bājai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The phone is ringing.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \mw{वो} \mw{फोन} \mw{बाज्यो}, \emph{vo phon bājyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{बाजणो}} (\emph{bājṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vādyate}, \textquotedblleft{}is made to sound\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists the Old Marwari verb \emph{bājaï}, \textquotedblleft{}to sound\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11513).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{संदेसो} (sandeso)}{संदेसो (sandeso)}]{\mw{संदेसो} (sandeso) — a message}

\label{lesson:MW-C197-sandeso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a phone number, then the Marwadi for to ring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{संदेसो}}
\textbf{\mw{संदेसो}} — \emph{sandeso} — \textquotedblleft{}a message\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हैं} \mw{संदेसो} \mw{सुण्यो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhaĩ sandeso suṇyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I listened to the message.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{संदेसो}} (\emph{sandeso}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{sandeśa}, \textquotedblleft{}message, information\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry, but lists Hindi \emph{sãdesā}, \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12904).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a phone number, then the Marwadi for to ring, then say \emph{sandeso} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मिटावणो} (miṭāvṇo)}{मिटावणो (miṭāvṇo)}]{\mw{मिटावणो} (miṭāvṇo) — to rub out; to delete}

\label{lesson:MW-C197-mitavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to ring, then the Marwadi for a message.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मिटावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{मिटावणो}} — \emph{miṭāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to rub out; to delete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{संदेसो} \mw{मत} \mw{मिटावो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sandeso mat miṭāvo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Don't delete the message.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{संदेसो} \mw{मिटायो}, \emph{mhaĩ sandeso miṭāyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मिटावणो}} (\emph{miṭāvṇo}) is the causative of a verb inherited from Sanskrit \emph{mṛṣṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}rubbed, wiped\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{miṭaï}, \textquotedblleft{}to be rubbed out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10299).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sandeso mat miṭāvo.} — Don't delete the message.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to ring, then the Marwadi for a message, then say \emph{miṭāvṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A Notice on the Door to A Call and a Message}

\label{lesson:MW-R197-review-191-197}



\begin{quote}
Say the Marwadi for a notice and a rule.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a notice, a rule, forbidden, careful, to obey
  \item danger, slowly, a pit, to print, to mend
  \item a rupee, a coin, a banknote, in cash, to pay
  \item to earn, to spend, a salary, a profit, credit
  \item a bank, a bank account, a debt, remaining, to be left over
  \item the post, an envelope, a parcel, an address, to send off
  \item a phone, a phone number, to ring, a message, to rub out
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A notice? (\textbf{\mw{सूचना}}, \emph{sūchnā}.) A rule? (\textbf{\mw{नियम}}, \emph{niyam}.) Forbidden? (\textbf{\mw{मना}}, \emph{manā}.) Careful? (\textbf{\mw{सावधान}}, \emph{sāvdhān}.) To obey? (\textbf{\mw{मानणो}}, \emph{mānṇo}.) Danger? (\textbf{\mw{खतरो}}, \emph{khatro}.) Slowly? (\textbf{\mw{धीरे}}, \emph{dhīre}.) A pit? (\textbf{\mw{खाड़ो}}, \emph{khāṛo}.) To print? (\textbf{\mw{छापणो}}, \emph{chhāpṇo}.) To mend? (\textbf{\mw{सुधारणो}}, \emph{sudhārṇo}.) A rupee? (\textbf{\mw{रुपियो}}, \emph{rupiyo}.) A coin? (\textbf{\mw{सिक्को}}, \emph{sikko}.) A banknote? (\textbf{\mw{नोट}}, \emph{noṭ}.) In cash? (\textbf{\mw{नगद}}, \emph{nagad}.) To pay? (\textbf{\mw{चुकावणो}}, \emph{chukāvṇo}.) To earn? (\textbf{\mw{कमावणो}}, \emph{kamāvṇo}.) To spend? (\textbf{\mw{खरचणो}}, \emph{kharchṇo}.) A salary? (\textbf{\mw{तनखा}}, \emph{tankhā}.) A profit? (\textbf{\mw{नफो}}, \emph{napho}.) Credit? (\textbf{\mw{उधार}}, \emph{udhār}.) A bank? (\textbf{\mw{बैंक}}, \emph{baiṅk}.) A bank account? (\textbf{\mw{खातो}}, \emph{khāto}.) A debt? (\textbf{\mw{करज}}, \emph{karaj}.) Remaining? (\textbf{\mw{बाकी}}, \emph{bākī}.) To be left over? (\textbf{\mw{बचणो}}, \emph{bachṇo}.) The post? (\textbf{\mw{डाक}}, \emph{ḍāk}.) An envelope? (\textbf{\mw{लिफाफो}}, \emph{liphāpho}.) A parcel? (\textbf{\mw{पारसल}}, \emph{pārsal}.) An address? (\textbf{\mw{ठिकाणो}}, \emph{ṭhikāṇo}.) To send off? (\textbf{\mw{मोकलणो}}, \emph{mokalṇo}.) A phone? (\textbf{\mw{फोन}}, \emph{phon}.) A phone number? (\textbf{\mw{नंबर}}, \emph{nambar}.) To ring? (\textbf{\mw{बाजणो}}, \emph{bājṇo}.) A message? (\textbf{\mw{संदेसो}}, \emph{sandeso}.) To rub out? (\textbf{\mw{मिटावणो}}, \emph{miṭāvṇo}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
